GitHub synchronization status: exact merged SHA confirmed

A blocked operation prints the exact reason, for example:

Integrated submission blocked: Approval or CI result belongs to a superseded patch set

docs.title: Retry, rollback, and recovery
docs.text:
Temporary Git, Gerrit SSH, network, and GitHub failures use bounded retries. On startup and after an event-stream reconnect, the worker queries every allowlisted component master tip and passes its exact merged change metadata through the normal idempotent uplift path. This permanently recovers a component merge event lost while Gerrit or CI was unavailable. The same reconciliation cycle compares integrated Gerrit and GitHub tips and recovers a missed guarded GitHub uplift. Unreachable module commits, unexpected paths, CI failures, missing labels, submit-policy failures, and merge conflicts are permanent for that event and are never converted to success.

After merge recovery, the same startup cycle queries configured verification targets. An active current patch set without a Verified vote from the CI account is rebuilt automatically, recovering an upload event lost during a restart. WIP changes wait for Mark As Active. An existing CI +1 or -1 is retained and is not run again.

Before submission, rollback means abandoning the open uplift change; the protected branch and GitHub are unchanged. After submission, use a normal reviewed Gerrit revert rather than rewriting history. GitHub synchronization is fast-forward only and can be retried after fixing credentials or connectivity.

For manual recovery:

  1. Read the last JSON changelog entry and the linked Gerrit CI log.
  2. Confirm the component SHA is on its Gerrit master branch.
  3. Confirm the integrated change's current patch set and submit requirements in Gerrit.
  4. Restart CI to reconcile the current component tip, or rerun the uplift command with the same exact metadata.
  5. If Gerrit is merged but GitHub is behind, restart CI. Startup reconciliation checks both branch tips.
  6. Never force-push either protected branch and never publish an unmerged patch set to GitHub.

docs.title: Administrator activation checklist
docs.text:
Repository code cannot safely perform these deployment operations automatically:

  1. Review and apply the generated xWalkPiCarAI ACL and submit requirements to refs/meta/config.
  2. Confirm Gerrit accepts the -has:unresolved submit expression on the installed Gerrit version.
  3. Add xwalk-ci with only read, review-upload, Verified, and submit permissions.
  4. Keep Code-Review +2 with authorized humans, or approve and provision a distinct automatic reviewer.
  5. Install mode-0600 SSH keys and pinned host keys through the CI credential store.
  6. Confirm the GitHub repository and protected master destination, then install its repository-scoped deploy key.
  7. Run one safe end-to-end test change before enabling automatic submit or GitHub push.

Until that checklist is completed and tested, automatic approval, automatic submission, and GitHub synchronization must be reported as configured but not operationally verified.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
https://github.com/TARS-v00-01 contains private, submitted-code mirrors of the xWalk Gerrit repositories. Gerrit remains the only development, review, and Submit system. GitHub is not a second writable source of truth, and GitHub pull requests are not the official review workflow.

Developer -> Gerrit review -> CI -> Code-Review +2 -> Submit -> replication -> TARS-v00-01 mirror

Pending patch sets and refs/changes/*, refs/drafts/*, refs/cache-automerge/*, refs/meta/*, refs/users/*, refs/edit/*, and refs/starred-changes/* are not replication destinations.

docs.title: Repository mapping
docs.text:
The machine-readable mapping is xWalk-rpi5-tool/py-agent/gerrit-tool/config/tars-mirror-map.tsv.

Gerrit project GitHub mirror xWalkPiCarAI TARS-v00-01/xWalkPiCarAI devloper-note TARS-v00-01/devloper-note xWalk-rpi5 TARS-v00-01/xWalk-rpi5 xWalk-rpi5-iw TARS-v00-01/xWalk-rpi5-iw xWalk-rpi5-tool TARS-v00-01/xWalk-rpi5-tool xWalkAgent TARS-v00-01/xWalkAgent xWalkAudioResources TARS-v00-01/xWalkAudioResources xWalkController TARS-v00-01/xWalkController xWalkHal TARS-v00-01/xWalkHal xWalkLibrary TARS-v00-01/xWalkLibrary xWalk-rpi5-trace TARS-v00-01/xWalk-rpi5-trace xWalkScheduler TARS-v00-01/xWalkScheduler xWalkIW TARS-v00-01/xWalkIW xWalk-rpi5-server TARS-v00-01/xWalk-rpi5-server

xWalkIW retains legacy submitted history. New active interface and tooling changes use xWalk-rpi5-iw and xWalk-rpi5-tool. xWalk-rpi5-server is reserved for the gRPC server and transport adapters. It cannot become a superproject gitlink until its first implementation commit is reviewed and submitted in Gerrit.

docs.title: Clone and update
docs.text:
Organization members clone the exact submitted integration tree with:

git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/TARS-v00-01/xWalkPiCarAI.git

Repair or initialize an existing clone with:

git submodule sync --recursive
git submodule update --init --recursive

The superproject uses organization-relative URLs. The exceptional Gerrit The Gerrit project and canonical GitHub repository both use devloper-note. Gerrit CI resolves its private checkout through the controlled helper.

docs.title: Developer workflow
docs.text:
Source the repository environment, change the owning component, run its host checks, and upload only to Gerrit:

source xWalk-git-env.sh
cd xWalk-rpi5-hw/xWalkHal
git switch master
git pull --ff-only origin master
git add <files>
git commit -s
git push origin HEAD:refs/for/master

origin is Gerrit. The optional github remote is fetch-only and has a non-routable push URL. Do not replace origin with GitHub, push a component branch to GitHub, or open a GitHub pull request as an alternate review.

After component Submit, update only its exact gitlink in xWalkPiCarAI. Run the complete integration checks and upload that pointer change for a separate Gerrit review and Submit.

docs.title: Replication installation
docs.text:
Use the replication plugin version matching Gerrit's API version. Gerrit 3.14.2 includes the compatible plugin inside its WAR. Install that exact JAR, then configure one explicit remote section per mapping. Do not use an uncontrolled project wildcard.

Each remote has these constraints:

  • one exact Gerrit project;
  • one exact private TARS-v00-01 repository;
  • only refs/heads/master:refs/heads/master;
  • no force marker in the refspec;
  • createMissingRepositories = false;
  • a repository-scoped deploy key; and
  • pinned GitHub host keys with strict checking.

The tracked examples are:

  • xWalk-rpi5-tool/py-agent/gerrit-tool/config/tars-replication.config.example;
  • xWalk-rpi5-tool/py-agent/gerrit-tool/config/tars-ssh.config.example; and
  • xWalk-rpi5-tool/py-agent/gerrit-tool/config/tars-mirror-map.tsv.

Reload after a configuration-only change:

ssh -p 29419 ADMIN@GERRIT_HOST gerrit plugin reload replication

Run an explicit idempotent verification pass with:

ssh -p 29419 ADMIN@GERRIT_HOST replication start --all --now --wait

docs.title: Credential rotation
docs.text:
Use one deploy key per GitHub repository. A private key is stored only in the Gerrit service account's mode-0600 SSH directory. Its public key is added to the matching GitHub repository with write permission.

Rotate a key without interrupting submitted-code replication:

  1. Generate a new repository-specific key outside every Git checkout.
  2. Add the new public key to the matching private GitHub repository.
  3. Add a temporary SSH alias that selects the new private key.
  4. Test authentication and an idempotent replication pass.
  5. Update the remote URL to the new alias and reload the plugin.
  6. Verify the Gerrit and GitHub master hashes are identical.
  7. remove the old deploy key from GitHub and securely retire its private key.

Never print, commit, copy into CI logs, or share a private key. Never replace a repository-scoped credential with an owner's personal token.

docs.title: GitHub Actions access
docs.text:
Private sibling submodules require a read-only credential. Store a fine-grained machine-account token as the organization or repository secret TARS_SUBMODULE_TOKEN. Limit it to repository contents read access for the mapped repositories. The checkout helper removes the temporary Git authorization header after recursive initialization.

Prefer a GitHub App installation token when the organization has an approved App. Do not use an owner's broad personal token.

docs.title: Developer-note artifact
docs.text:
The xWalkPiCarAI GitHub workflow builds developer documentation only after the exact submitted integration commit has reached the private GitHub mirror. It runs xWalk-rpi5-tool/doc-tool/wiki.sh verify and uploads the generated build-devloper-note-wiki/github-site directory as a private Actions artifact. The artifact name contains the run ID and attempt number, is retained for 30 days, and is visible only to accounts authorized for the private repository.

This workflow is a post-replication verification and distribution step. It does not upload a Gerrit patch set, replicate a branch, publish a Pages site, or push any repository ref. Gerrit remains the source of the submitted commit and its review record. The GitHub workflow run identifies the mirrored commit that produced the artifact.

The current organization plan does not support GitHub Pages for the private integration repository. GitHub returns 404 when actions/configure-pages queries an unconfigured Pages site and returns a plan-related 422 when an administrator attempts to create it. Keep the repository private. Do not add pages: write, id-token: write, actions/configure-pages, actions/upload-pages-artifact, or actions/deploy-pages merely to suppress the error.

Enabling Pages later requires all of the following:

  1. an organization plan that supports Pages for this private repository;
  2. an approved privacy review of the rendered documentation and component links;
  3. Pages configured with Source: GitHub Actions by an authorized administrator; and
  4. a reviewed and submitted Gerrit change that restores the least-privilege workflow permissions and deployment.

Until then, organization members retrieve documentation from the matching private Actions run. Public users receive neither the artifact nor private component source.

docs.title: Optional global organization wiki
docs.text:
GitHub reserves https://tars-v00-01.github.io/ for an organization site published from a repository named exactly TARS-v00-01/tars-v00-01.github.io. With the current plan, that repository must be public. GitHub does not provide private access control for an organization site. The repository, rendered site, downloaded assets, search index, sitemap, and embedded metadata must therefore be reviewed as public content. This global site is an optional future publication target and is not part of the current mirror mapping.

Do not publish the private developer-note artifact directly to the global site. If public documentation is approved, create a distinct Gerrit project containing only the sanitized documentation source and map that one project explicitly to TARS-v00-01/tars-v00-01.github.io. Before creating either repository, approve its canonical name, visibility, content policy, responsible team, and rollback owner.

The public documentation review must reject:

  • credentials, tokens, keys, authentication headers, and protected configuration values;
  • private Gerrit, CI, GitHub, or infrastructure addresses;
  • private source files, generated source archives, or component repository contents;
  • internal-only architecture, deployment, incident, account, and recovery details;
  • links that disclose inaccessible private paths or query parameters; and
  • unreviewed Git commit identifiers or component metadata not approved for public release.

The only permitted publication path is:

sanitized docs -> Gerrit patch set -> documentation CI -> review -> Submit -> exact GitHub mirror -> Pages deploy

Pending patch sets must not reach GitHub. GitHub Actions may deploy the exact mirrored submitted revision but must not commit, push, rewrite history, or accept pull requests as the official review path. Gerrit must receive separate change-log rows for mirror status and Pages deployment status, including the GitHub commit and deployment links. The documentation CI result is reused for both publication records; creating two targets must not execute the same quality graph twice.

If private browser access is required, do not use an organization site. Continue using private Actions artifacts, host the wiki behind authenticated college infrastructure, or obtain GitHub Enterprise Cloud approval for a private project Pages site. A private project site uses a GitHub-assigned URL and is not the global organization root.

docs.title: Validation and troubleshooting
docs.text:
Run local structure checks with:

xWalk-rpi5-tool/shell-agent/gerrit-tool/validate-tars-mirrors.sh

With authenticated private-repository access, also verify every pinned commit and excluded review ref:

xWalk-rpi5-tool/shell-agent/gerrit-tool/validate-tars-mirrors.sh --remote

If replication fails:

  1. confirm the Gerrit plugin is enabled and API-compatible;
  2. validate replication.config with git config --file;
  3. confirm the project has one exact remote section and master-only refspec;
  4. test the remote's SSH alias with BatchMode=yes;
  5. confirm the deploy key belongs only to the matching repository;
  6. verify GitHub host keys are pinned;
  7. inspect Gerrit's replication log without printing credentials; and
  8. retry the exact project with replication start PROJECT --now --wait.

A rejected non-fast-forward indicates divergence. Stop and investigate; never force-push either side.

docs.title: Repository rules and current limitation
docs.text:
All repositories are private. xwalk-admins has administrative access; xwalk-developers and xwalk-readers are read-only. Repository descriptions identify the Gerrit authority and submit-gated mirror role.

Private-repository rulesets and protected-branch enforcement require a GitHub plan that supports those features. Until that plan is available, organization team permissions and repository-scoped deploy keys reduce access, but an organization owner still has administrative push capability. Owners must not use that capability for normal development.

After upgrading the plan, create an active default-branch ruleset that:

  • restricts updates and deletions;
  • blocks non-fast-forward pushes;
  • grants bypass only to repository deploy keys or the approved GitHub App; and
  • grants no ordinary human or pull-request merge bypass.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
Before a Gerrit Submit, abandon or revise the pending change. GitHub is unchanged because review refs are not replicated.

After Submit, create and submit a normal Gerrit revert. Replication then fast-forwards the revert commit to GitHub. Never reset, delete, or force-push a published mirror branch.

To suspend replication without rewriting history:

  1. disable the affected remote section or the plugin;
  2. reload the plugin;
  3. preserve queued-event and replication logs;
  4. repair credentials or mapping;
  5. compare Gerrit and GitHub branch hashes; and
  6. resume with an idempotent exact-project replication pass.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This page contains the normal Git commands for the multi-repository xWalk workspace. Run commands from the repository indicated by each section.

Gerrit is the development and review system. GitHub is a submitted-code mirror. Never push a developer commit, pending patch set, integration pointer, branch, or tag directly to GitHub.

The workspace has two Git layers:

  • MyPiCarX is the xWalkPiCarAI superproject. It records exact component commits as Git submodule metadata, also called gitlinks.
  • devloper-note, xWalk-rpi5-iw, xWalk-rpi5-tool, and the component directories below xWalk-rpi5-hw are independent repositories.

Commit a source change in its owning component repository. Do not include a pending component commit in the superproject. After the component change is submitted, the automatic integration uplift creates the reviewed superproject gitlink update.

docs.title: Enter the workspace
docs.text:
cd /repo/joxjoh24/MyGitCode/MyPiCarX

Load the project Git environment in every new Bash session:

source xWalk-git-env.sh

Show the configured Gerrit endpoint, repository, branch, CI location, and submodules:

xwalk_git_env_show

Show the available project Git helper commands:

xwalk_git_env_help

docs.title: Configure identity
docs.text:
Inspect the effective identity:

git config user.name

git config user.email

Configure the identity for the current repository when it is missing:

git config user.name "YOUR NAME"

git config user.email "YOUR EMAIL"

Use an identity registered in Gerrit. Do not store passwords, tokens, private keys, cookies, or authenticated URLs in Git configuration committed to the repository.

docs.title: Install the Gerrit commit hook
docs.text:
Each independent repository needs Gerrit's commit-msg hook before its first commit. Enter the repository that will own the change, load the project Git environment, and install the hook into that repository's actual Git directory:

scp -P "$GERRIT_SSH_PORT" "$GERRIT_USER@$GERRIT_HOST:hooks/commit-msg" "$(git rev-parse --git-path hooks/commit-msg)"

chmod 0755 "$(git rev-parse --git-path hooks/commit-msg)"

This form works in the superproject and in a submodule whose .git entry is a gitfile. The hook adds the stable Change-Id Gerrit uses to associate later patch sets with the same review.

docs.title: Clone and initialize
docs.text:
Organization members may clone the submitted private integration mirror:

git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/TARS-v00-01/xWalkPiCarAI.git MyPiCarX

Enter the clone and load the Git environment:

cd MyPiCarX

source xWalk-git-env.sh

The environment preserves GitHub as a read-only fetch source and configures normal uploads for Gerrit. Verify every remote before development:

git remote -v

Initialize an existing clone that does not yet have its submodules:

git submodule sync --recursive

git submodule update --init --recursive

Do not use git submodule update --remote. That command can move a component beyond the exact submitted commit reviewed in the superproject.

docs.title: Inspect the complete workspace
docs.text:
Show concise status for the superproject and every real submodule:

xwalk_git_status

Show the superproject status:

git status --short --branch

Show all pinned and checked-out submodule commits:

git submodule status --recursive

Show configured paths, URLs, branches, and actual gitlinks:

xwalk_git_modules

Show the current superproject commit:

git log -1 --oneline --decorate

Show the commit currently recorded for one submodule:

git rev-parse HEAD:xWalk-rpi5-tool

Show the commit checked out inside that submodule:

git -C xWalk-rpi5-tool rev-parse HEAD

The two hashes must match in a clean synchronized checkout.

docs.title: Update submitted superproject metadata and submodules
docs.text:
Run these commands from the MyPiCarX root after an integration uplift is submitted:

git pull --ff-only

git submodule sync --recursive

git submodule update --init --recursive

Verify the result:

git status

git submodule status --recursive

git pull --ff-only updates the submitted superproject metadata. git submodule sync --recursive applies reviewed .gitmodules URL changes. git submodule update --init --recursive checks out the exact commits recorded by the new gitlinks.

docs.title: Understand modified: SUBMODULE (new commits)
docs.text:
The message below does not mean that source files are uncommitted:

modified: xWalk-rpi5-tool (new commits)

It means the submodule checkout is at a different commit from the gitlink recorded by the current superproject commit. This normally occurs after a local component commit and before its submitted integration uplift is pulled.

Inspect both commits:

git rev-parse HEAD:xWalk-rpi5-tool

git -C xWalk-rpi5-tool rev-parse HEAD

After the component and automatic integration reviews are submitted, run the three update commands from the previous section. To return immediately to the currently pinned commit without deleting the component branch, run:

git submodule update --init --recursive -- xWalk-rpi5-tool

This may leave the submodule checkout detached at the reviewed gitlink. Use it only when the local component work is already committed or otherwise safe.

docs.title: Start work in a component repository
docs.text:
Enter the owning component. This example uses xWalk-rpi5-tool:

cd /repo/joxjoh24/MyGitCode/MyPiCarX/xWalk-rpi5-tool

Confirm that the component worktree is clean:

git status --short --branch

Fetch its submitted Gerrit branch:

git fetch origin master

Switch to the local component branch:

git switch master

Fast-forward to the submitted branch:

git merge --ff-only origin/master

Inspect recent history before editing:

git log --oneline --decorate --max-count=10

docs.title: Review local changes
docs.text:
Show changed paths:

git status --short

Show unstaged changes:

git diff

Show staged changes:

git diff --cached

Check whitespace errors:

git diff --check

Show a summary:

git diff --stat

Inspect one file:

git diff -- path/to/file

docs.title: Stage and commit a component change
docs.text:
Stage only reviewed paths:

git add path/to/file another/path/to/file

Confirm the exact staged change:

git diff --cached --check

git diff --cached

Create a signed commit using the standard xWalk subject format:

git commit -s -m "[xWalk-NNN][RPI5] Describe the change"

The installed Gerrit commit-msg hook adds a stable Change-Id. Confirm the message, sign-off, and Change-Id before upload:

git log -1 --format=full

docs.title: Upload a new Gerrit review
docs.text:
From the owning component, upload an active review to master:

git push origin HEAD:refs/for/master

The project helper performs the same upload and selects the current repository:

xwalk_gerrit_push "$PWD" master origin

An active upload starts the owning module's Gerrit CI.

Upload work in progress without starting normal active-review CI:

git push origin HEAD:refs/for/master%wip

The equivalent helper is:

xwalk_gerrit_push_wip "$PWD" master origin

Use Gerrit's Mark As Active action when the WIP patch set is ready. That transition triggers CI for the current patch set.

docs.title: Update an existing Gerrit change
docs.text:
Keep the existing Change-Id. Edit the files, stage them, and amend the commit:

git add path/to/updated-file

git commit --amend --no-edit

Upload again using the same review ref:

git push origin HEAD:refs/for/master

Gerrit creates a new patch set in the same change because the Change-Id remains unchanged. Never replace the Change-Id when updating a review.

docs.title: Rebase a Gerrit change
docs.text:
For a conflict-free server-side rebase, open the Gerrit change and select Rebase. Gerrit creates a new patch set and reloads the review.

If Gerrit reports a merge conflict, check out the local component and rebase onto the submitted branch:

git fetch origin master

git rebase origin/master

List conflicted files:

git status

After resolving one or more conflicts, stage the resolved paths:

git add path/to/resolved-file

Continue the rebase:

git rebase --continue

Abort the rebase and return to the pre-rebase state when the conflict must be reconsidered:

git rebase --abort

After a successful local rebase, verify that the original Change-Id remains in the commit and upload the new patch set:

git log -1 --format=full

git push origin HEAD:refs/for/master

Do not use git push --force. Gerrit patch-set upload does not require it.

docs.title: Fetch a Gerrit patch set for inspection
docs.text:
Use the exact fetch command from the change's Download menu. A patch-set ref has this form:

refs/changes/NN/CHANGE_NUMBER/PATCH_SET

Fetch the selected ref through the component's Gerrit remote:

git fetch origin refs/changes/NN/CHANGE_NUMBER/PATCH_SET

Inspect it without moving the component branch:

git switch --detach FETCH_HEAD

Return to the component branch:

git switch master

docs.title: After Gerrit Submit
docs.text:
Confirm the component's submitted branch contains the reviewed commit:

git fetch origin master

git log -1 --oneline origin/master

Do not manually commit the component pointer in xWalkPiCarAI while an automatic integration uplift is pending. Wait for the uplift review to pass complete integration CI, receive approval, and be submitted. Then update the root checkout:

cd /repo/joxjoh24/MyGitCode/MyPiCarX

git pull --ff-only

git submodule sync --recursive

git submodule update --init --recursive

docs.title: Safe staging and recovery commands
docs.text:
Remove a path from the staging area without discarding its working-tree edit:

git restore --staged path/to/file

Temporarily save tracked and untracked local work only when the owner intends to restore it later:

git stash push --include-untracked -m "temporary xWalk work"

List saved work:

git stash list

Restore the latest saved work and retain the stash if conflicts occur:

git stash apply

Remove that stash only after verifying the restored work:

git stash drop

Abort an unfinished merge:

git merge --abort

Abort an unfinished cherry-pick:

git cherry-pick --abort

Never discard someone else's work. Do not use git reset --hard, destructive clean commands, force pushes, or branch deletion as routine recovery actions.

docs.title: Remote and publication checks
docs.text:
Show fetch and push destinations:

git remote -v

Confirm that the GitHub remote cannot accept direct pushes:

git remote get-url --push github

The expected push URL is the local no-push guard:

xwalk-gerrit-uplift-only://direct-github-push-disabled

Compare the local branch with its configured Gerrit upstream:

git status --short --branch

Show local commits not yet present in the upstream branch:

git log --oneline @{upstream}..HEAD

Show submitted upstream commits not yet present locally:

git log --oneline HEAD..@{upstream}

docs.title: Final clean-check sequence
docs.text:
Run from the superproject root after submitted metadata and submodules are updated:

git status --short --branch

git submodule status --recursive

xwalk_git_status

A clean result has no modified paths, and every submodule status line begins with a space. A leading + means the checked-out component differs from the recorded gitlink, - means the submodule is uninitialized, and U means a gitlink merge conflict must be resolved.

docs.title: Commands prohibited by project policy
docs.text:
Do not use these publication patterns:

git push github ...
git push --force ...
git push --mirror ...
git submodule update --remote

Development changes go to refs/for/master in Gerrit. GitHub receives only submitted branches through the configured synchronization service.

docs.title: xWalk Developer Notes Wiki
docs.text:
xWalk-rpi5-tool/doc-tool/wiki.sh builds these Markdown collections as a searchable Material for MkDocs website. It provides local-development, college-server, and GitHub artifact profiles.

Run the examples from the repository root. Generated dependencies and HTML remain under the ignored build-devloper-note-wiki directory.

docs.title: Local profile
docs.text:
Build the wiki, bind it only to the current computer, and open the default browser:

xWalk-rpi5-tool/doc-tool/wiki.sh local

The default URL is http://127.0.0.1:8000/. Press Ctrl-C to stop the local server.

Serve locally without opening a browser:

xWalk-rpi5-tool/doc-tool/wiki.sh local --no-open

Choose another loopback port:

xWalk-rpi5-tool/doc-tool/wiki.sh local --port 8001

The local profile rejects non-loopback bind addresses.

docs.title: College-server profile
docs.text:
Run this command on the college server:

xWalk-rpi5-tool/doc-tool/wiki.sh server

It builds production-style static HTML under build-devloper-note-wiki/server-site, binds to 0.0.0.0:8080, and serves until Ctrl-C is pressed.

When the college provides a public HTTPS address, include it in the build:

xWalk-rpi5-tool/doc-tool/wiki.sh server --site-url https://docs.example.edu/xwalk/

Use another approved port when required:

xWalk-rpi5-tool/doc-tool/wiki.sh server --port 9000 --site-url https://docs.example.edu/xwalk/

Binding to 0.0.0.0 listens on every server interface. Worldwide access additionally requires:

  • a public college DNS name or public IP address;
  • firewall and NAT rules that permit the selected port;
  • a TLS certificate and HTTPS reverse proxy, normally Nginx or Apache;
  • college authorization for public hosting; and
  • a persistent service manager if the wiki must survive logout or reboot.

The built-in Python static server is appropriate for initial verification. Use the college's managed HTTPS web server for production access and point its document root at the generated server-site content.

docs.title: GitHub artifact profile
docs.text:
Build the same static documentation artifact used by GitHub Actions:

xWalk-rpi5-tool/doc-tool/wiki.sh github

The default site URL embedded in locally generated metadata is:

https://TARS-v00-01.github.io/xWalkPiCarAI/

Open the configured site URL after building:

xWalk-rpi5-tool/doc-tool/wiki.sh github --open

This option does not open the local artifact. With Pages disabled, the configured URL may return 404.

Override the URL when the repository or custom domain changes:

xWalk-rpi5-tool/doc-tool/wiki.sh github --site-url https://docs.example.org/xwalk/

The github profile only creates build-devloper-note-wiki/github-site; it never pushes. After an approved Gerrit integration commit is submitted and synchronized to TARS-v00-01/xWalkPiCarAI/master, the developer-note-pages.yml workflow builds the site once and uploads it as a private GitHub Actions artifact. Authorized organization members can download the artifact from the workflow run. The artifact is retained for 30 days and does not publish a website.

The current GitHub plan does not support Pages for the private xWalkPiCarAI repository. Do not make the repository public to enable Pages because the integration tree identifies private component revisions. A future Pages deployment requires an approved organization plan, an explicit privacy review, and a reviewed Gerrit change that restores Pages permissions and deployment steps. Until all three conditions are satisfied, a Pages API 404 or plan-related 422 is an expected configuration limitation, not a reason to bypass Gerrit or repository privacy.

The workflow validates the committed integration metadata without initializing private Gerrit submodules. The developer-note sources are already part of the exact submitted integration commit synchronized to GitHub, so the artifact build requires no Gerrit SSH key, server address, or account variables.

docs.title: Optional global organization wiki
docs.text:
A global organization site can use this URL:

https://tars-v00-01.github.io/

GitHub requires its repository to be named exactly TARS-v00-01/tars-v00-01.github.io. With the current plan, that repository must be public. An organization Pages site cannot be restricted to organization members, so the complete site and every published asset must be treated as public. Creating the repository is not approved merely by documenting this option, and the global site is not currently configured.

If a global site is approved, publish only a sanitized documentation set from a separate Gerrit project. Exclude private source, credentials, internal service addresses, restricted architecture details, and links that reveal content unavailable to public readers. Keep all component repositories and the integration repository private.

The approved flow must remain submit-gated:

sanitized documentation -> Gerrit review and CI -> Submit -> explicit mirror -> TARS-v00-01/tars-v00-01.github.io -> Pages

The GitHub repository must not accept normal developer pushes or pull requests as an alternate review path. The Gerrit change log must record the submitted source revision, mirror result, GitHub commit link, and Pages deployment result. A failed deployment is corrected through a new Gerrit review; it is never repaired with a direct GitHub push.

docs.title: CI verification
docs.text:
Validate wiki-owned local links, strictly build the GitHub artifact, and validate its homepage, sitemap, search-index JSON, and configured site URL:

xWalk-rpi5-tool/doc-tool/wiki.sh verify

This non-serving command is used by Gerrit component CI, integrated Host Quality, and GitHub Host Quality. It does not open a browser, bind a port, or publish the generated artifact.

docs.title: Dependency setup
docs.text:
Every profile creates an isolated Python environment when needed. Prepare it without starting a site:

xWalk-rpi5-tool/doc-tool/wiki.sh setup

The package pin is in xWalk-rpi5-tool/doc-tool/requirements-wiki.txt. First-time installation requires Python 3, the Python venv module, and package-index access.

docs.title: Remove generated files
docs.text:
xWalk-rpi5-tool/doc-tool/wiki.sh clean

This removes only the validated build-devloper-note-wiki directory. It does not remove source notes.

docs.title: Build behavior
docs.text:
• mkdocs.yml enables Material navigation, tables, heading anchors, and local full-text search.
  • Every profile stages a fresh copy of the Markdown source before building or serving it.
  • Links to workspace files outside devloper-note are converted in the staged artifact to GitHub source links for the exact deployed revision. Source Markdown retains its checkout-relative links.
  • Every build cleans stale HTML from its profile-specific site directory.
  • Generated environments and HTML must not be committed.

docs.title: xWalk C++ Documentation Index
docs.text: This index links the current C++ architecture and module documentation. Module-specific contracts, build options, backend ownership, safety constraints, and verification commands remain in each module README.

docs.title: Workspace architecture
docs.text:
• xWalk common library: shared interface target for public headers in xWalk-rpi5-hw/xWalkLibrary/common.
  • xWalkHal: aggregate hardware-abstraction architecture and build options.
  • xWalkAgent: application coordinators and aggregate Agent verification.
  • xWalkController: standalone CLI aggregate and Controller composition.
  • High-level architecture: workspace layers and ownership rules.
  • Hardware architecture: devices and backends.
  • CLI architecture: command coverage and implementation plan.
  • Raspberry Pi deployment guide: install layout, idempotent setup, board-profile checks, and narrowly scoped device permissions.
  • CMake dependency guide: external libraries, imported targets, build-mode requirements, package names, and discovery troubleshooting.
  • xWalk-rpi5-tool overview: tool inventory, safety classes, and detailed links.
  • Gerrit account setup guide: account provisioning, dedicated SSH keys, repository setup, review upload, voting, and remote-network access.
  • Add a user to a Gerrit repository: individual account creation, group-based project access, SSH onboarding, verification, and revocation.
  • Create Gerrit and configure xWalk CI: new server installation, project permissions, CI service identity, worker configuration, and first-run verification.
  • Device Tree overlay guide: asset roles and inspection.
  • Release acceptance checklist: independent host, ARM package, plug-and-run, and physical-safety evidence gates.
  • Raspberry Pi 5 and PiCar-X readiness audit: hardware matrix, demonstrated support boundaries, deployment requirements, blockers, and safe first tests.
  • Host production readiness work: host sanitizer, stress, coverage, clean-environment, and staged-install verification.
  • Language-model provider configuration: Ollama, ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, credential handling, and model selection.
  • Licence-key workflow: authenticated encryption, protected input, environment loading, deployment, and secret-handling boundaries.
  • Audio resources: combined sound-effect and background-music assets, provenance, layout, and integrity hashes.

docs.title: Scripts
docs.text:
• Clean build script guide: safe discovery, preview, confirmation, and removal of generated CMake and Python output.
  • Dependency installer script flags: complete option, default, compatibility alias, combination, and exit-status reference.
  • Hardware provisioning script guide: Robot HAT profile and Linux device validation with configuration persistence.
  • Host coverage script guide: foreground configure, build, test, coverage reporting, and enforced thresholds.
  • Raspberry Pi setup script guide: safe dry-run, target validation, privileged apply behavior, and troubleshooting.
  • xWalk licence tool guide: protected input, authenticated encryption, serial generation, decryption, output, and exit behavior.
  • xWalk environment loader guide: sourced-shell loading, template validation, temporary-file cleanup, and environment security.

docs.title: Robot HAT board diagram
docs.text: The diagram identifies the Robot HAT power, motor, PWM, ADC, digital, I2C, SPI, UART, button, and speaker connections. See Hardware introduction for the corresponding hardware notes.

docs.title: Agent modules
docs.text:
• xWalkHandler: controller contract, parsing, and command handlers.
  • xWalkApp: executable targets, process entry points, generated help, application tests, and Raspberry Pi composition.
  • Controller command flow: Mermaid traces from every CLI command through boot selection, typed handlers, Agent and HAL services, and final endpoints.
  • PiCar-X Controller command reference: copyable commands for preflight, driving, sensing, media, voice, calibration, and SPI diagnostics.
  • Jarvis and Gemini configuration: local Ollama, optional Gemini credentials, Piper voice setup, configuration, validation, and safe startup.
  • xWalk licence installation: encrypted model configuration, credential loading, Controller validation, safe startup, and troubleshooting.
  • xWalkBoot: host stub and RPi process hardware ownership.
  • xWalkLineTracking: bounded line following.
  • xWalkPicarx: movement, calibration, and sensing.
  • xWalkSelfDrive: gestures, sounds, and action queue.
  • xWalkSpiTransfer: bounded SPI transactions.
  • xWalkVoiceActiveCar: sensor-aware voice car.
  • xWalkGptCar: upstream JSON GPT-car assistant.

docs.title: HAL modules
docs.text:
The HAL source tree groups low-level platform interfaces and common services under interface, hardware device abstractions under device, sensor and actuator components under sensor, and higher-level robot services and features under layer1.

  • xWalkAdc: Robot HAT analog-to-digital conversion.
  • xWalkAdxl345: ADXL345 acceleration sensing.
  • xWalkAudio: shared ALSA PCM, mixer, and device ownership.
  • xWalkBoardControl: board reset, discovery, and firmware data.
  • xWalkBuzzer: active and passive buzzer control.
  • xWalkConfig: configuration parsing and persistence.
  • xWalkGpio: GPIO abstraction and Linux backend.
  • xWalkGPT: speech coordination plus Vosk and Espeak providers.
  • xWalkI2c: I2C abstraction and Linux backend.
  • xWalk-rpi5-iw: I2C and Controller Protobuf DTOs and typed gRPC services.
  • xWalkLanguageModel: provider-neutral language-model access.
  • xWalkLed: GPIO and PWM LED control.
  • xWalkLineTracker: grayscale line-position estimation.
  • xWalkMotor: single and paired motor control.
  • xWalkMusic: musical tones and injected audio playback.
  • xWalkPwm: Robot HAT PWM output.
  • xWalkRobot: coordinated multi-servo robot control.
  • xWalkServo: calibrated servo positioning.
  • xWalkSpeaker: decoded audio-file playback.
  • xWalkSpi: bounded SPI abstraction and Linux backend.
  • xWalk-rpi5-trace/README.md: filtered callback-based diagnostics.
  • xWalkUltrasonic: ultrasonic distance measurement.
  • xWalkUserButton: button events and press timing.
  • xWalkUtils: platform utilities and bounded lazy caching.
  • xWalkVoiceAssistant: speech and model backend composition.

docs.title: Safety and verification
docs.text: Use host tests for ordinary verification. Raspberry Pi hardware tests are opt-in and must only run when the correct Raspberry Pi and Robot HAT are connected, the robot is secured, and physical execution is approved. Use ctest -N -L hardware to list hardware tests without executing them.

docs.title: XWalkAdc
docs.text: XWalkAdc acquires raw samples from one MCU ADC channel and converts samples to volts. The caller creates and retains the referenced XWalkI2c object.

docs.title: Public interface
docs.text:
The authoritative declaration is xHal_Rpi5CarAdc.h.

  • Construct with an I2C reference, channel, and optional device address.
  • read() returns one raw sample assembled from exactly two bytes.
  • readVoltage() converts the sample using the 3.3-volt reference and 4095 maximum count.

Valid channels are 0 through 7. Backend failures and malformed response lengths are reported through the documented exception contracts.

docs.title: XWalkTrace
docs.text: XWalkTrace provides filtered diagnostic output through an append-only log file and an injected callback. It replaces implicit console logging with explicit, testable sinks.

docs.title: Public interface
docs.text:
The authoritative declarations are in the xWalk-rpi5-trace/README.md module document.

The application configures the active severity and supplies the callback context. The trace object appends accepted records to <build-directory>/log/xWalkTrace.log, independent of the process working directory, and does not own the additional callback destination.

docs.title: XWalkConfigStore and XWalkConfig
docs.text:
XWalkConfigStore provides flat key-value persistence. XWalkConfig provides section-aware configuration persistence. Both are defined by the xWalkConfig module.

Configuration objects own their paths and in-memory values. Filesystem access passes through common file wrappers. Deployment owns directory creation, permissions, and recovery policy.

Applications should load and validate configuration before constructing motor, servo, or robot components. Hardware classes do not open configuration files.

docs.title: XWalkI2c
docs.text: XWalkI2c is the hardware-independent callback-driven bus abstraction. XWalkI2cLinux optionally owns a Linux I2C file descriptor.

docs.title: Public interface
docs.text:
See xWalkI2c and the public headers under its core and hardware include directories.

Create the backend before XWalkI2c, pass its pointer and callback bridges to the constructor, and keep it alive until all dependent ADC, PWM, firmware, and sensor objects are destroyed. Serialize transactions that share a bus.

docs.title: XWalkUltrasonic
docs.text: Uses caller-created trigger and echo XWalkGpio objects. Successful results are in centimetres; documented negative values distinguish timeout and invalid pulse measurements. See xWalkUltrasonic.

docs.title: XWalkAdxl345
docs.text: Uses a caller-created XWalkI2c object to acquire raw and converted acceleration data. See xWalkAdxl345.

docs.title: XWalkLed and XWalkRgbLed
docs.text: XWalkLed controls one GPIO LED. XWalkRgbLed coordinates three non-owning PWM pointers. See xWalkLed.

docs.title: XWalkBuzzer
docs.text: Supports active GPIO and passive PWM operation without owning either dependency. See xWalkBuzzer.

docs.title: XWalkGrayscaleModule and XWalkLineTracker
docs.text: The grayscale component calibrates three ADC channels. The line tracker derives channel status and normalized line position. See xWalkLineTracker.

docs.title: XWalkUserButton
docs.text: Interprets active-low button events and bounded press timing through a caller-created GPIO dependency. See xWalkUserButton.

docs.title: XWalkMotor and XWalkMotors
docs.text: XWalkMotor controls one motor using the PWM and direction dependencies selected for the board mode. XWalkMotors coordinates two non-owning motor pointers.

docs.title: Public interface
docs.text:
See xWalkMotor and its two public class headers.

Speed commands use the documented range from -100 to 100 percent. Validate coordinated commands before changing either motor. Apply zero output before destroying dependencies or changing hardware configuration.

docs.title: XWalkMusic
docs.text: XWalkMusic provides music-theory conversion, PCM tone generation, and injected audio operations. It does not own an ALSA device or launch a platform process.

docs.title: Public interface
docs.text:
See xWalkMusic and xHal_Rpi5CarMusic.h.

The application supplies audio callbacks and keeps callback contexts valid for the complete object lifetime. Validate note names, tempo, duration, volume, and sample properties using the ranges documented in the header.

docs.title: XWalkPwm and XWalkPwmTimerState
docs.text: XWalkPwm controls one MCU PWM channel. XWalkPwmTimerState coordinates the frequency and period shared by channels assigned to one hardware timer.

docs.title: Public interface
docs.text:
See xWalkPwm, xHal_Rpi5CarPwm.h, and timer-state header.

Create one timer-state object before all PWM channels that use it. A frequency change that conflicts with an active sibling channel is rejected. Pulse values must remain within the configured period.

docs.title: XWalkGpio
docs.text: XWalkGpio provides digital mode, pull, polarity, value, and edge operations. XWalkGpioLinux is the optional Linux resource-owning backend.

docs.title: Public interface
docs.text:
See xWalkGpio, GPIO header, and the Linux backend header when building for Raspberry Pi.

The application owns callback context lifetime. Keep interrupt callbacks short, non-blocking, and free from filesystem, network, speech, or playback operations.

docs.title: XWalkRobot
docs.text: XWalkRobot coordinates caller-created servo objects, named positions, and multi-servo action frames. Persistent configuration remains in XWalkConfig.

docs.title: Public interface
docs.text:
See xWalkRobot and xHal_Rpi5CarRobot.h.

Create servo objects in main() and pass validated non-owning pointers through the robot configuration. Keep every servo and its PWM dependency alive longer than the robot object.

docs.title: XWalkServo
docs.text: XWalkServo translates angle and pulse-duration commands into a caller-created XWalkPwm output.

docs.title: Public interface
docs.text:
See xWalkServo and xHal_Rpi5CarServo.h.

The default configuration uses 50 hertz, a 4095-count period, angles from -90 to 90 degrees, and pulse widths from 500 to 2500 microseconds. Confirm the mechanical range before commanding an attached servo.

docs.title: C++ speech interfaces
docs.text:
XWalkTextToSpeech coordinates text synthesis through an injected backend. XWalkSpeechToText coordinates recognition through an injected backend. Both classes belong to xWalkGPT.

The C++ core owns no model, microphone, audio device, network client, process, credential, or generated media file. The application supplies and owns those facilities and keeps callback contexts valid for the object lifetime.

The Linux hardware layer supplies two offline providers. XWalkSpeechRecognizerVosk loads libvosk.so and one configured model at runtime, while XWalkTextToSpeechEspeak executes Espeak without a shell and converts its WAV output to signed sixteen-bit PCM. ALSA adapters perform microphone capture and shared speaker playback. xWalkBootRpi retains Robot HAT speaker power for the complete synthesis and playback lifetime.

docs.title: C++ utility interfaces
docs.text:
The xWalkUtils module contains:

  • XWalkUtils for injected platform utility and output operations;
  • XWalkLazyReader<ValueType> for bounded-rate callback value caching;
  • XWalkStderrGuard for scope-bound stderr suppression and restoration.

Generic utilities do not create hardware or platform services. Callers provide callbacks and contexts explicitly. Common non-member functions remain in the xwalk::hal::common namespace under xWalkLibraryCommon.

docs.title: C++ API reference
docs.text:
The public C++ headers are authoritative. This index groups the xWalk HAL modules by responsibility.

Responsibility Module documentation Common types and free functions xWalk common library I2C xWalkI2c GPIO xWalkGpio ADC xWalkAdc PWM xWalkPwm Servo xWalkServo Motors xWalkMotor Sensors Sensors and actuators Robot coordination xWalkRobot Board services xWalkBoardControl Configuration xWalkConfig Audio and speech Music and speech Diagnostics and utilities Trace and utilities

Create platform backends and component objects in main(). Pass dependencies by reference; consuming classes retain documented non-owning pointers.

docs.title: Add a User to a Gerrit Repository
docs.text: This guide explains how a Gerrit administrator gives one person access to an existing xWalk repository. Access is granted through Gerrit groups and project ACLs. Never give a user direct filesystem access to $GERRIT_SITE/git, and never share the administrator or xwalk-ci account.

docs.title: Required information
docs.text:
Collect these values before making changes:

Value Source GERRIT_SERVER_HOST xWalk-rpi5-tool/py-agent/gerrit-tool/config/gerrit-setup.conf GERRIT_SSH_PORT xWalk-rpi5-tool/py-agent/gerrit-tool/config/gerrit-setup.conf GERRIT_ADMIN_USER xWalk-rpi5-tool/py-agent/gerrit-tool/config/gerrit-setup.conf PROJECT_NAME Gerrit project list or the installer configuration PROJECT_BRANCH Protected review branch, normally master USERNAME Unique lowercase login selected for the person USER_EMAIL The person's individual email address

The administrator must already have a registered SSH key and must be able to run this command:

ssh -p GERRIT_SSH_PORT GERRIT_ADMIN_USER@GERRIT_SERVER_HOST gerrit version

Replace every uppercase token in the examples. Do not paste unresolved tokens into a real command.

docs.title: Create the web login
docs.text:
Run the installed xWalk-rpi5-tool account helper on the Gerrit server:

$HOME/bin/gerrit-user-add USERNAME

Enter a unique password of at least 12 characters. The helper stores only a bcrypt hash, reloads Caddy, and rolls back the user-file change if the reload fails. Send the password to the user through an approved private channel. Do not put it in Git, email, a command argument, or a remote URL.

Ask the user to sign in once through the configured HTTPS URL. The first successful login creates the Gerrit account associated with that HTTP identity.

docs.title: Set the Gerrit identity
docs.text:
After the first sign-in, assign the person's name and email through the administrator SSH connection:

ssh -p GERRIT_SSH_PORT GERRIT_ADMIN_USER@GERRIT_SERVER_HOST gerrit set-account --full-name 'USER FULL NAME' --add-email USER_EMAIL USERNAME

Never assign two people the same username or email. Each account must remain attributable to one person.

docs.title: Add the user to an access group
docs.text:
Gerrit repository access comes from groups. Use the smallest group that provides the required permissions:

Group Intended access Developers Read and upload patch sets to refs/for/PROJECT_BRANCH Reviewers Read, comment, and vote within the configured Code-Review range Project-Owners Project ACL administration, final review, and Submit Service Users Restricted automation accounts such as xwalk-ci

An ordinary contributor normally needs Developers. Add Reviewers only when the person is authorized to vote. Do not add a developer to Project-Owners, Service Users, or Gerrit's Administrators group.

ssh -p GERRIT_SSH_PORT GERRIT_ADMIN_USER@GERRIT_SERVER_HOST gerrit set-members --add USERNAME Developers

If review voting is also required:

ssh -p GERRIT_SSH_PORT GERRIT_ADMIN_USER@GERRIT_SERVER_HOST gerrit set-members --add USERNAME Reviewers

Verify the resulting membership:

ssh -p GERRIT_SSH_PORT GERRIT_ADMIN_USER@GERRIT_SERVER_HOST gerrit ls-members Developers

Open Projects → List → PROJECT_NAME → Access and confirm that the selected group has only the intended permissions. A normal developer may push to refs/for/refs/heads/PROJECT_BRANCH; they must not receive direct Push, Force Push, Create Reference, Submit, or Verified voting permission on the protected branch.

docs.title: Register the user's SSH key
docs.text:
The user generates a dedicated key on their own computer:

ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_xwalk_gerrit -C "USER_EMAIL"

The private key remains on that computer. The user signs in to Gerrit, opens Settings → SSH Keys, and adds only ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_xwalk_gerrit.pub.

Test the connection from the user's computer:

ssh -p GERRIT_SSH_PORT USERNAME@GERRIT_SERVER_HOST

Gerrit should print its welcome message and state that interactive shells are disabled.

docs.title: Clone and upload for review
docs.text:
Clone the repository and install Gerrit's commit-msg hook:

git clone ssh://USERNAME@GERRIT_SERVER_HOST:GERRIT_SSH_PORT/PROJECT_NAME

cd PROJECT_NAME && scp -P GERRIT_SSH_PORT USERNAME@GERRIT_SERVER_HOST:hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod 755 .git/hooks/commit-msg

After making and testing a change, upload it for review:

git push origin HEAD:refs/for/PROJECT_BRANCH

The commit message must contain a Change-Id. Component changes are uploaded only to Gerrit master; they are never pushed directly to GitHub.

docs.title: Verify and revoke access
docs.text:
Confirm that the user can read the intended project and upload a harmless review change, but cannot push directly to the protected branch or set Verified.

When access is no longer required:

  1. Remove the user from every project group in Gerrit.
  2. Revoke their SSH keys and deactivate the Gerrit account.
  3. Disable the proxy login on the Gerrit server.
$HOME/bin/gerrit-user-disable USERNAME

Disabling the web login alone does not revoke existing Gerrit SSH access. Complete all three steps.

See Gerrit Account Setup Guide for the developer-side SSH configuration, review workflow, voting meanings, and network-access guidance.

docs.title: About the battery
docs.text: The documented Robot HAT battery input accepts a balanced two-cell lithium-ion pack in the 6.0-to-8.4-volt range through an XH2.54 three-pin connector.

docs.title: Electrical characteristics
docs.text:
Property Documented value Cell count Two 18650 cells Nominal capacity 2,000 milliampere-hours Energy 14.8 watt-hours Connector XH2.54 three-pin Over-discharge protection 6.0 volts

ADC channel A4 measures the divided battery voltage. The board uses a 20-kilohm and 10-kilohm divider, so the battery voltage is three times the ADC pin voltage. XWalkBoardControl::batteryVoltage() performs this conversion.

Use a compatible balanced pack and never treat software measurement as the only battery-protection layer.

docs.title: xWalk CLI architecture and HAL integration plan
docs.text:
Project: xWalk Firmware

Executable: xwalk-picarx-control

Owning modules: xWalk-rpi5-hw/xWalkController/xWalkHandler, xWalk-rpi5-hw/xWalkController/xWalkApp, and xWalk-rpi5-hw/xWalkAgent/xWalkPlatform/xWalkBoot

Document date: 2026-08-02

Status: Current implementation plus proposed integration plan

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
This document describes the implemented CLI architecture, its current commands, the Raspberry Pi object graph, HAL module coverage, modules that are not yet exposed, and a staged plan for safely adding them.

The plan is architectural guidance. Commands marked as proposed do not exist until their code, help, tests, CMake wiring, deployment configuration, and safe backend composition are implemented.

docs.title: 2. Source layout
docs.text:
xWalk-rpi5-hw/xWalkAgent/xWalkPlatform/xWalkBoot/
├── core/include/                       shared boot lifecycle and service types
├── core/src/                           shared one-shot boot lifecycle
├── hardware/include/                   Raspberry Pi boot contract
├── hardware/src/                       Raspberry Pi composition root
├── stub/include/                       device-free host-stub contract
├── stub/src/                           device-free host-stub implementation
├── stub/test/include/                  host-only fixture declarations
└── stub/test/src/                      deterministic host lifecycle coverage
xWalk-rpi5-hw/xWalkAgent/xWalkVoice/xWalkLocalVoiceChatbot/
├── include/                            chatbot contract and application callbacks
├── src/                                foreground loop and response filtering
└── test/src/                           deterministic voice-pipeline coverage
xWalk-rpi5-hw/xWalkAgent/xWalkVoice/xWalkVoiceActiveCar/     sensor, wake-word, speech, response, and action coordination
xWalk-rpi5-hw/xWalkAgent/xWalkVoice/xWalkVoiceActiveCarGpt/  English Buddy language profile
xWalk-rpi5-hw/xWalkAgent/xWalkVoice/xWalkGptCar/             upstream JSON GPT-car profile
xWalk-rpi5-hw/xWalkController/xWalkHandler/
├── include/xController.h         parser and coordinator contract
├── include/xControllerTypes.h    callback and sound-operation types
├── src/xControllerLifecycle.cpp  dependency and callback binding
├── src/common/                                shared command-safety support
├── src/vehicle/                               movement and sensing handlers
├── src/vision/                                camera and visual-control handlers
├── src/voice/                                 speech and language-model handlers
├── src/media/                                 sound and background-music handlers
├── src/connectivity/                          application-control and SPI handlers
├── src/calibration/                           calibration and verification handlers
├── src/platform/                              passive platform handlers
└── test/src/xControllerTest.cpp  deterministic handler coverage
xWalk-rpi5-hw/xWalkController/xWalkApp/
├── CMakeLists.txt                              executable targets and CTest registration
├── activate/include/                          command-activation declarations
├── activate/src/                              validated command routing and usage
├── activate/resources/help.json               generated help source
├── boot/include/                              boot and application-support declarations
├── boot/src/                                  callbacks, boot selection, and runner
├── cli/hardware/src/xControllerMain.cpp       Raspberry Pi entry and boot composition
├── cli/host/src/                              host entry and host-stub lifecycle
├── parse/include/xControllerParsing.h         typed parser declarations
├── parse/src/                                 option, command, request, and output parsing
└── test/src/xControllerAppTest.cpp isolated host-application GoogleTest
xWalk-rpi5-hw/xWalkController/xWalkConfig/
├── picar-x.conf                               manifest and mutable overrides
└── picar-x.d/                                 functional and AI-provider fragments

The CLI imports the Agent aggregate. Its Raspberry Pi executable links xWalkBootRpi, which privately owns board control, Linux I2C and GPIO, ALSA, native audio decoding, and command-specific Agent services.

Controller-owned headers and sources use the compact xController<Component> filename convention. Generic shared types are qualified through ctrl::; Agent coordinator types use agent::, while hardware-specific contracts stay qualified through hal::. Build and editor metadata must reference the compact filenames so removed xAgent_Rpi5CarController<Component> paths do not survive in compilation databases.

Both executables use XWALK_parseControllerApplicationArguments() from parse/src/xControllerApplicationArguments.cpp. This gives host and Raspberry Pi builds one validation contract for deployment and resource options. Host main delegates its complete behavior to XWALK_runHostControllerApplication(); Raspberry Pi main retains only signal installation, resource validation, boot-mode selection, and hardware composition.

docs.title: 3. Request lifecycle
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Shell
    participant Main
    participant Boot as XWalkBootRpi
    participant Graph as Command backend graph
    participant Cli as XWalkController
    participant Agent
    participant HAL

    Shell->>Main: process arguments
    alt help only
        Main-->>Shell: generated help, no backend boot
    else operational command
        Main->>Boot: select mode and construct automatic object
        Main->>Boot: run context and application callback
        Boot->>Boot: consume one object run attempt
        Boot->>Graph: construct selected resources
        Graph->>Cli: construct with available services
        Cli->>Agent: validate and execute command
        Agent->>HAL: bounded hardware or service calls
        HAL-->>Shell: result through CLI output callback
    end

Help is returned before backend boot. It does not open I2C, claim GPIO, start ALSA, move hardware, or contact an external provider.

docs.title: 4. One-shot boot contract
docs.text: XWalkBootRpi::run() accepts a context and synchronous application callback. The object marks itself started before claiming hardware. A successful, failed, or throwing callback consumes that object's only run attempt. Backend objects remain local to run() and live until the command callback returns. They are destroyed in reverse order before run() returns, and the automatic boot object is destroyed when main() exits.

docs.title: 5. CLI callback boundary
docs.text:
XWalkControllerCallbacks supplies synchronous application operations:

Callback Current Raspberry Pi implementation Output Writes one line to standard output Input Writes a prompt and reads standard input Delay Calls the shared millisecond sleep facility Continue line tracking Reads signal-controlled foreground state Sound Routes through boot-owned Music and the native libsndfile/ALSA backend

The callback context is non-owning. All callbacks must remain valid for the CLI lifetime.

docs.title: 6. Current command surface
docs.text:
Command Actions or required values Current implementation move forward, backward PiCar-X motor coordination turn left, right Steering plus bounded movement sequence cam pan, tilt Camera-servo positioning sensor distance, grayscale Ultrasonic and grayscale acquisition spi transfer plus hexadecimal bytes SPI-only full-duplex transaction line-track start, stop Foreground line-tracking Agent self-drive One preset action SelfDrive Agent and ALSA music sound play, volume, music, stop Native WAV/MP3 decoding and ALSA playback voice-chat start, stop Local voice-chat service boundary voice-active-car start, stop Sensor-aware voice-car service boundary voice-active-car-gpt start, stop English Buddy voice-car profile gpt-car start, stop plus source flags Upstream JSON GPT-car profile voice-controlled-car start, stop Wake-word movement-control service boundary voice-prompt-car start, stop Spoken movement-demonstration service boundary calibrate No subcommand Interactive steering, pan, and tilt calibration

Movement speed is limited to 100 percent. Steering is limited to 30 degrees. Camera pan and tilt use their documented mechanical command ranges. Movement sequences stop the motors after successful completion.

docs.title: 7. Self-drive action names
docs.text:
The CLI publishes shell-friendly names and converts hyphens to the exact Agent action name:

shake-head
nod
wave-hands
resist
act-cute
rub-hands
think
twist-body
celebrate
depressed
forward
backward
honking
start-engine

Separate action words remain compatible, such as self-drive wave hands. The Agent performs final validation before hardware changes.

docs.title: 8. Raspberry Pi composition
docs.text:
The current operational path performs these steps:

  1. Discover the Robot HAT through XWalkDevice.
  2. Create XWalkI2cLinux and the callback-driven XWalkI2c front end.
  3. Create reset and speaker GPIO objects retained for the boot callback.
  4. Create battery ADC A4 and retained XWalkBoardControl, then reset the MCU.
  5. Keep board control alive so voice playback retains speaker-enable ownership.
  6. Create shared PWM timer state and pan, tilt, and steering servos.
  7. Create D2 and D3 GPIO objects for ultrasonic acquisition.
  8. Create ADC A0, A1, and A2 plus XWalkGrayscaleModule.
  9. Create XWalkUltrasonic and the PiCar-X configuration store.
  10. Create the board-specific motor graph.
  11. Create XWalkPicarx from the complete caller-owned graph.
  12. Create a command-specific Agent and backend graph when required.
  13. Construct XWalkController last and dispatch the command.

docs.title: 8.1 Board-specific motor branch
docs.text: Robot HAT v5 creates four PWM channels: P12, P13, P14, and P15. A legacy board creates P13 and P12 plus D4 and D5 direction GPIO lines.

docs.title: 8.2 Line-tracking branch
docs.text: Only a line-track command creates XWalkLineTracking. start installs SIGINT and SIGTERM handlers and runs bounded steps in the foreground until cancellation. stop performs an immediate stop in the current process. It does not control a separate CLI process.

docs.title: 8.3 Self-drive branch
docs.text: Only a self-drive command creates XWalkAudioAlsa, XWalkMusicAlsa, native decoding, XWalkMusic, and XWalkSelfDrive. A sound command creates the same audio graph without SelfDrive. This keeps the mixer and PCM owner out of unrelated command paths.

docs.title: 8.4 Voice branches
docs.text: Voice commands select dedicated boot modes and publish typed Agent service boundaries. The direct movement behaviors live in xWalkVoiceActiveCar: XWalkVoiceControlledCar recognizes “hey robot”, movement words, and “sleep”; XWalkVoicePromptCar speaks and runs the four-movement demonstration. The Raspberry Pi composition loads the configured Vosk library and model, captures microphone PCM through ALSA, and publishes XWalkSpeechToText. The prompt path runs Espeak without a shell, parses its PCM WAV output, plays it through the shared ALSA owner, and publishes XWalkTextToSpeech while Robot HAT speaker power remains claimed. The application callback constructs the Agent with these boot-owned HAL services and signal-aware callbacks. Voice chat and voice-active commands additionally compose Ollama and XWalkVoiceAssistant; voice-active commands add Music, SelfDrive, the status LED, and XWalkCameraCapture. The camera Agent calls the backend-neutral camera HAL, while deployment selects CSI through rpicam-still or USB V4L2 through ffmpeg.

docs.title: 9. Current HAL coverage
docs.text:
The coverage terms used here are:

  • Command: directly visible to the CLI user.
  • Internal: composed only as a dependency of another command.
  • Partial: some module behavior is exposed, but significant public behavior is not.
  • Missing: no current CLI composition or user command.
Module Coverage Current use xWalkI2c Internal Bus for PiCar-X hardware xWalkGpio Internal Reset, speaker, LED, ultrasonic, and legacy motor direction xWalkSpi Command spi transfer through an SPI-only boot graph xWalkPwm Internal Servos and motors xWalkAdc Internal Grayscale and temporary battery ADC xWalkCamera Internal Voice-active still-image input through CSI or USB xWalkServo Partial Camera, steering, and calibration only xWalkMotor Partial PiCar-X movement only xWalkLineTracker Partial Grayscale module only; the tracker class is not composed xWalkUltrasonic Command sensor distance xWalkConfig Partial PiCar-X calibration store only xWalkBoardControl Partial Device discovery, MCU reset, and speaker power xWalkAudio Internal Music, sound, and voice capture/playback xWalkMusic Command Self-drive actions and sound playback or volume xWalkAdxl345 Missing No accelerometer command xWalkLed Internal Voice-active-car status indication xWalkBuzzer Missing No buzzer command xWalkRobot Missing No robot action or servo-frame command xWalkUserButton Missing No button state or bounded monitor command xWalkSpeaker Missing Sound commands use Music rather than Speaker xWalkGPT Command Vosk recognition and Espeak synthesis for voice-car commands xWalkLanguageModel Internal Configured HTTP model for voice-chat and voice-active commands xWalkVoiceAssistant Command Complete pipeline for voice-chat and voice-active commands xWalk-rpi5-trace Missing No trace configuration or output composition xWalkUtils Missing No platform-information or utility commands

xWalkLibraryCommon is used throughout but is not itself an operational CLI feature.

docs.title: 10.1 Fully absent from the command graph
docs.text:
The following completed HAL modules have no current CLI command or composition:

  • xWalkAdxl345;
  • xWalkBuzzer;
  • xWalkRobot;
  • xWalkUserButton;
  • xWalkSpeaker;
  • xWalk-rpi5-trace;
  • xWalkUtils.

docs.title: 10.2 Partially covered modules
docs.text:
• xWalkBoardControl lacks battery, firmware, speaker-enable, and speaker-disable commands.
  • xWalkMusic lacks tone, pause, and resume commands.
  • xWalkAudio has no explicit user-facing device or mixer selection.
  • xWalkConfig is limited to the PiCar-X calibration path.
  • xWalkLed is composed only as voice-active status output and has no direct command.
  • xWalkLanguageModel is composed through Ollama but has no direct model command.
  • xWalkServo and xWalkMotor are exposed only through PiCar-X operations.
  • raw I2C, GPIO, PWM, and ADC diagnostics are intentionally not exposed.

docs.title: 11. CLI expansion principles
docs.text:
New integration should preserve these rules:

  1. Parse enough of the command before constructing a hardware graph.
  2. Compose only the backend and HAL objects required by that command.
  3. Keep help and read-only syntax discovery free of hardware and network access.
  4. Store optional services as nullable, non-owning dependencies.
  5. Return status 3 with a clear unavailable message when a required service is not composed.
  6. Keep provider credentials, model endpoints, devices, and pin roles in deployment configuration.
  7. Keep line-track limited to start and stop.
  8. Make long-running operations foreground, bounded, and cancellable.
  9. Validate all coordinated outputs before the first physical mutation.
  10. Add host tests before opt-in hardware tests.

docs.title: 12. Proposed command organization
docs.text:
The following names are proposals for implementation planning. They are not current commands.

Proposed group Proposed actions HAL modules board info, battery, firmware, speaker-on, speaker-off BoardControl accelerometer read ADXL345 led on, off, rgb, blink, stop LED and RGB LED buzzer on, off, tone Buzzer robot position, action, move, stop, reset Robot button state, monitor UserButton music play, pause, resume, stop, volume, tone Music and Audio sound Existing actions Speaker, Music, and Audio adapters speech listen, transcribe, speak, stop GPT and Audio model prompt, instructions, clear LanguageModel and Ollama voice-assistant run, stop VoiceAssistant, GPT, model, and audio platform info, ip, user, executable, volume Utils trace level Trace config get, set, write, reload Config

Raw i2c, gpio, pwm, and adc mutation commands should not be added to the normal robot CLI. If field diagnostics require them, place them under a separately built diagnostic executable with explicit allowlists, pin and channel restrictions, and stronger safety prompts.

docs.title: 13. Service injection design
docs.text:
The current CLI has constructor overloads for PiCar-X, line tracking, and self-drive. Continuing with one constructor per combination will not scale to all HAL modules.

A future implementation should introduce a documented, non-owning service aggregate owned by the application. For example, it may contain nullable pointers to board, speaker, music, speech, model, voice, robot, button, utility, and diagnostic coordinators. The aggregate must not allocate or own these services.

flowchart LR
    MAIN[RPi composition root]
    SERVICES[Non-owning CLI services]
    CLI[XWalkController]
    BOARD[Board service]
    AUDIO[Audio service]
    SPEECH[Speech service]
    MODEL[Model service]
    ROBOT[Robot service]

    MAIN --> BOARD
    MAIN --> AUDIO
    MAIN --> SPEECH
    MAIN --> MODEL
    MAIN --> ROBOT
    BOARD --> SERVICES
    AUDIO --> SERVICES
    SPEECH --> SERVICES
    MODEL --> SERVICES
    ROBOT --> SERVICES
    SERVICES --> CLI

This is a proposed reusable convention and must be reviewed against the coding guide before implementation. Until approved, focused constructor overloads remain the established pattern.

docs.title: 14. Command implementation structure
docs.text:
Each command handler has one source file, grouped by its owning functionality:

xWalk-rpi5-hw/xWalkController/xWalkApp/activate/src/                             command activation and routing
xWalk-rpi5-hw/xWalkController/xWalkApp/parse/src/                                typed parsing and output formatting
xWalk-rpi5-hw/xWalkController/xWalkApp/boot/src/                                 boot selection and service composition
xWalk-rpi5-hw/xWalkController/xWalkHandler/src/common/                                       shared safety support
xWalk-rpi5-hw/xWalkController/xWalkHandler/src/vehicle/                                      movement and sensing
xWalk-rpi5-hw/xWalkController/xWalkHandler/src/vision/                                       camera and vision
xWalk-rpi5-hw/xWalkController/xWalkHandler/src/voice/                                        voice and AI
xWalk-rpi5-hw/xWalkController/xWalkHandler/src/media/                                        audio operations
xWalk-rpi5-hw/xWalkController/xWalkHandler/src/connectivity/                                 external control
xWalk-rpi5-hw/xWalkController/xWalkHandler/src/calibration/                                  calibration operations
xWalk-rpi5-hw/xWalkController/xWalkHandler/src/platform/                                     platform diagnostics

Every XWALK_handler... method remains isolated in its own translation unit. XWALK_runPicarxControllerCommand() is a separate application free function with friend access to route commands without publishing protected handlers. Each file retains complete function documentation and is listed explicitly in the controller CMake target.

docs.title: Completed foundation
docs.text:
• The stale aggregate dependency has been removed, so the HAL source tree and CMake graph agree.
  • sound uses boot-owned native decoding, XWalkMusic, shared ALSA output, and retained speaker power.
  • Voice chat and voice-active commands compose Vosk, Espeak, ALSA, the configured model backend, and XWalkVoiceAssistant.
  • Host tests remain the default verification path; Raspberry Pi tests are discovery-only without approval.

docs.title: Phase 2: add read-only board and sensor commands
docs.text:
Add the lowest-risk commands first:

  • board info from XWalkDevice;
  • board battery from XWalkBoardControl;
  • board firmware from XWalkFirmwareInfo;
  • accelerometer read from XWalkAdxl345;
  • button state from a caller-selected input without starting its worker;
  • read-only platform information from XWalkUtilsLinux.

Avoid resetting the MCU for commands that only need discovery or direct sensor access. Split the current eager PiCar-X graph so a read-only board command does not create motors, servos, or ultrasonic GPIO lines.

Completion gate: help remains device-free and each command has deterministic host values and failure coverage.

docs.title: Phase 3: add bounded actuator commands
docs.text:
Add LED and buzzer before multi-servo robot actions:

  1. Compose exact GPIO or PWM dependencies only after action validation.
  2. Require bounded duration for blink and tone commands unless an explicit off command is guaranteed.
  3. Apply inactive output during construction and normal command completion.
  4. Add robot commands only after servo channel configuration and safe poses are deployment-controlled.
  5. Make robot stop and robot reset safe, idempotent operations.

Do not expose unrestricted pin or PWM channel selection through user input.

Completion gate: host tests prove validation precedes mutation and every timed action reaches an inactive state.

docs.title: Phase 4: expose configuration and diagnostics
docs.text:
Add narrowly scoped configuration keys rather than arbitrary filesystem paths. Proposed behavior:

  • config get reads allowlisted deployment or calibration fields;
  • config set validates a typed value in memory;
  • config write performs explicit persistence;
  • trace level changes one caller-owned trace object;
  • platform volume uses the approved mixer backend.

Do not add a general shell-command action even though XWalkUtilsLinux supports process execution. The normal robot CLI must not become an arbitrary command launcher.

Completion gate: paths, keys, values, and process behavior are allowlisted and covered by host tests.

docs.title: Phase 5: add speech recognition and synthesis
docs.text:
Add command-local speech graphs:

  • speech listen creates ALSA capture and one configured recognizer;
  • speech transcribe uses a validated bounded input path and the recognizer;
  • speech speak creates board speaker power, one synthesizer, and ALSA playback;
  • speech stop cancels recognition in the current foreground process.

Device names, recognizer, synthesizer, language, credentials, timeouts, and maximum PCM sizes are deployment configuration. Do not print microphone samples, credentials, or synthesized PCM.

Completion gate: fake-provider host tests pass and target tests require explicit device and privacy approval.

docs.title: Phase 6: add language-model commands
docs.text:
Compose XWalkLanguageModelOllama only for a model or voice-assistant command. Require an explicit endpoint, model, timeout, maximum history, and prompt-size limit.

model prompt should perform one bounded synchronous request. Instructions and history operations should use the same process-local model owner. A one-shot executable cannot preserve history between separate invocations unless a deployment-approved persistent history service is added.

Completion gate: host tests use fake transport, no test contacts a network, and logs omit prompt content by default.

docs.title: Phase 7: compose the voice assistant
docs.text:
For voice-assistant run, create dependencies in this order:

  1. board discovery, speaker GPIO, ADC, and board control;
  2. shared ALSA owner;
  3. ALSA capture and recognizer, then XWalkSpeechToText;
  4. Ollama backend, then XWalkLanguageModel;
  5. synthesizer and ALSA playback, then XWalkTextToSpeech;
  6. XWalkVoiceAssistant;
  7. CLI command adapter.

Run one round by default. Any repeated mode must be foreground, signal-cancellable, and bounded between rounds. Wake-word detection is not part of the current HAL and requires a separately reviewed backend.

Completion gate: an end-to-end host test covers silence, recognized input, model response, synthesis, playback, stop, and all unavailable-provider paths.

docs.title: Phase 8: add bounded event monitoring
docs.text:
button monitor may start the XWalkUserButton worker only after callbacks and signal cancellation are ready. Print event names, not unbounded diagnostics. Stop and join the worker before GPIO destruction.

Do not use button callbacks to invoke blocking speech, model, filesystem, or playback operations directly. Queue a bounded application event instead.

Completion gate: host tests cover Ctrl+C cancellation, callback lifetime, long press, and clean joining.

docs.title: 16. CMake integration plan
docs.text:
For each command family:

  1. Keep the neutral CLI library free of Linux headers.
